posts.title: Good Morning San Diego: Padres should be willing to trade pieces to improve roster
posts.description: SAN DIEGO, CA - OCTOBER 06: Freddy Fermin #54 of the San Diego Padres looks on from the dugout prior to Game Three of the National League Division Series presented by Booking.com between the Milwaukee Brewers and the San Diego Padres at Petco Park on Tuesday, October 6, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Rob Tringali/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The San Diego Padres have found themselves in a position to be a trade partner with other teams in MLB due to their depth at catcher and the bullpen. The Padres have Freddy Fermin, Luis Campusano and Ethan Salas behind the plate and it is unlikely they carry all three catchers throughout the season. The free agent catching market is limited so it gives San Diego an opportunity to work a deal for other major league talent or minor league talent that will improve the farm system. posts.title: Back-end starter continues to build on underrated San Diego tenure
posts.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Randy Vasquez #98 of the San Diego Padres pitches against the Arizona Diamondbacks during the first inning at Petco Park on September 27, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Randy Vásquez Vásquez was an under-the-radar piece in the blockbuster trade between the Padres and the New York Yankees for superstar Juan Soto. posts.title: Good Morning San Diego: Free agent urgency increases with lockout looming
posts.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 05: General manager A. J. Preller of the San Diego Padres looks on during NLDS Workouts at Petco Park on October 05, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is now or never for the San Diego Padres — well, maybe not never, but the Padres have to address their roster with Dec. 1 just days away which could result in a lockout. San Diego has been rumored to be “in” on multiple players but those rumors have proven to be just that to this point in the offseason. The problem is the Padres are getting a reputation for being linked to players who often end up signing elsewhere, which leads some to believe that players and agents are using the franchise to boost their contract lengths and values in other markets. Padres general manager A.J.
